# Independent transaction capacity review

No actionable defect found in this bounded change. A 4 MiB plan limit is sufficient for the measured full adoption plan; a 16 MiB journal limit provides reasonable finite headroom while preserving the existing failure/residual reporting behavior. This is workload-specific assurance, not a guarantee for every permitted plan or unlimited retries.

The read-only actual plan contains 48 steps and serializes canonically to 1,967,815 bytes (46.9% of the new plan limit). Its control-plane evidence is 1,146,627 bytes, its largest planned state is 10,022 bytes, and the sum of each step's largest before/after state is 108,587 bytes. The production validator accepts it under the changed bound. [real-plan-observation.json](real-plan-observation.json) binds these measurements to the exact input hash; the input's machine paths are not copied into this review. No real transaction was executed by the reviewer.

Source review confirms that only the plan and journal constants change. Nesting, 128-step, 256 KiB state, path ownership, phase ordering, continuous transitions, immutable evidence, hash-chain, lock/race and explicit recovery-authority checks remain. Plan rejection precedes lock/journal creation. Journal appends remain bounded and durable before effects; failed completion recording still returns observed residuals and any journal error rather than claiming completion. The reader's finite allocation grows from approximately 8 to 16 MiB; nothing becomes unbounded.

Independently reran `node --test tests/migration-transaction.test.mjs`: **19 passed, zero failed or skipped**. [transaction-tests.log](transaction-tests.log) retains this execution. The new 3 MiB fixture performs actual file/journal IO, fails after exposure, resumes without duplicating exposure, and restores original manager/selection/staging state under explicit fixture recovery authority. The oversized fixture rejects a 4 MiB evidence field plus plan overhead before creating a journal or recording an adapter effect. Existing mutation, recovery, corrupt-journal, ownership, race and final-inspection controls also pass.

Limits: the 3 MiB fixture uses five operational phases with synthetic bound evidence, not the actual 48-step machine transaction. Its journal does not exhaust the new 16 MiB ceiling. Actual backup records and repeated residual observations determine eventual journal size; a generic plan with many maximal backup observations or arbitrarily many retries can still exhaust it. Existing truthful failure behavior remains essential. Final full-suite, rebuilt acceptance, patch publication and actual machine update belong to the parent and are not certified by this review.

Four passes: inspect the changed constants and surrounding effect/recovery boundaries; independently measure/validate the actual plan; inspect and execute real file-transaction regression controls; challenge capacity/memory/universal-guarantee claims and bind the evidence. No source edit, model request, commit or actual-home mutation was performed.
